Rahul (Finance): FYI 1: new procurement advisory rolling out for Q3 spend. Main points: centralized review for sponsorships > $10k, travel cards limited to $2k per trip, and vendor onboarding requiring certificate of insurance for engagements > $30k. Effective Mon Jun 14. Full memo: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/FIN/pages/Q3+Spend+Advisory :mega:

Marta (Marketing): Quick q 1 - our conference sponsorship is $12k and includes booth + meals. Does that trigger the centralized review?

Rahul (Finance): Yes, sponsorships >= $10k go to centralized review. Please file a procurement ticket and attach the sponsorship package + expected deliverables. We need event ROI justification for approvals.

Chen (DevRel): For booth logistics (shipping, onsite power), if we spend < $2k on incidental costs can we use the PCard?

Rahul (Finance): Incidental event expenses under $2k total can use PCard. Anything above should go on the ticket under "event expenses". Also please avoid splitting the same expense across multiple cards to bypass review.

Sasha (Accounting): Note on travel: travel cards are capped at $2k per trip for lodging + per diem. For multi-city trips submit a travel approval form so we can consider exception. Receipts required for reimbursements.

procure-bot: procurement ticket created: FIN-2026-7789 by Marta (Marketing) 1 1 status: intake queued.

Marta (Marketing): I filed FIN-2026-7789 with the sponsorship deck and budget. We have 6 weeks to confirm. Anything else you need?

Rahul (Finance): Please include the expected attendee list, lead-gen targets, and PM sign-off. If the vendor requires insurance (they often do for exhibitor activities), you'll need the COI; procurement will request it when routing.

Chen (DevRel): For vendor onboarding > $30k, what sort of insurance are we asking for? General liability or professional liability?

Rahul (Finance): Typically general liability + cyber liability if they'll handle any data. We'll specify required limits on the ticket. If vendor cannot provide COI, Legal may require indemnity language or escrow.

Sasha (Accounting): For payment timing: sponsorships invoiced upfront should have a PO attached and be sent to ap@redwood.com with PO#. If billing is split, indicate invoice schedule in the ticket. Late POs can delay recognition.

Marta (Marketing): Got it. I'll add the ROI doc and COI if vendor provides it.

Rahul (Finance): One more: were adding a weekly procurement digest for spend > $5k to help teams catch pending approvals. If you see your ticket in the digest and need priority, reply in the thread with [PRIORITY] and a short reason.

Chen (DevRel): Thanks 1 saved the page.

Sasha (Accounting): I'll update the PO template to include COI and insurance fields so requests are complete at intake.
